task_instruction: Rewrite each direct wh-question as a reported question.
paragraphs: After watching Jurassic Park at a neighborhood cinema, Mia and Alex go to a cafe and talk about dinosaurs. Alex asks Mia to share what she remembers from science class. Alex asked Mia, {{red:Which dinosaur did you find most interesting?}} {{mask_1}} Mia said she had been fascinated by Triceratops. Alex asked, {{red:What do you know about its horns?}} {{mask_2}} Mia explained that scientists study the skull and fossils to understand what the horns may have been used for.

They compare different kinds of dinosaurs. Alex asked Mia, {{red:How large was a Tyrannosaurus rex?}} {{mask_3}} Mia said its size varied, and that fossil evidence helped scientists estimate it. Alex asked, {{red:What did herbivorous dinosaurs eat?}} {{mask_4}} Mia answered that many ate plants. Alex asked, {{red:Where have paleontologists found dinosaur fossils?}} {{mask_5}} Mia said fossils had been discovered on several continents.

Alex opens a science article on his phone. He asked Mia, {{red:Why do scientists compare fossils from different places?}} {{mask_6}} Mia explained that comparisons could reveal similarities and differences between species. Alex asked, {{red:When did the Jurassic Period begin?}} {{mask_7}} Mia said it began millions of years ago, long before humans existed. Alex asked, {{red:Which period came after the Jurassic Period?}} {{mask_8}} Mia replied that the Cretaceous Period followed it.

The friends discuss how researchers learn about extinct animals. Alex asked Mia, {{red:How can a fossil show the shape of an animal's teeth?}} {{mask_9}} Mia said that a fossilized jaw could preserve the tooth shapes. Alex asked, {{red:What were scientists studying when they found the new fossil?}} {{mask_10}} Mia said they were examining rock layers. Alex asked, {{red:Who discovered the fossil at the site?}} {{mask_11}} Mia read that a field team had found it. Alex asked, {{red:How long had the fossil been buried?}} {{mask_12}} Mia said that the researchers were still studying the rock around it.

Alex asks about popular ideas in dinosaur movies. He asked Mia, {{red:Why do filmmakers use sound effects for dinosaurs?}} {{mask_13}} Mia said that sound effects could make a scene feel dramatic. Alex asked, {{red:What can movie effects tell us about real dinosaur sounds?}} {{mask_14}} Mia replied that movies could not prove exactly what the animals sounded like. Alex asked, {{red:How do paleontologists decide whether a dinosaur walked on two legs?}} {{mask_15}} Mia said they studied bones and fossil tracks. Alex asked, {{red:Which details in a film are based on scientific evidence?}} {{mask_16}} Mia said that some details were inspired by research, while others were invented for the story.

Before they leave, Alex asks Mia what she wants to learn next. Alex asked Mia, {{red:What would you like to study about dinosaurs?}} {{mask_17}} Mia said she would like to learn how different species lived in their environments. Alex asked, {{red:Where will you look for reliable information?}} {{mask_18}} Mia said she would read museum and university resources. Alex asked, {{red:Who is giving a talk about fossils at the museum next week?}} {{mask_19}} Mia checked the event page and found the speaker's name. At the door, Alex asked, {{red:When are you going to visit the exhibit?}} {{mask_20}} Mia said she planned to go the following Saturday.
